summary: The last day: It is the last day, and {the ones left behind} ask {the one who leaves} what comes next.
realLife: One life: In sixth grade Joe's family left Hong Kong for the U.S. The friends wrote weekly at first and then lost touch; decades later Pak, who kept every letter, found Joe, and they now bike and eat together weekly. Another: A five-year-old Army child moving from Virginia to Alabama made a list of people to hug and have sign it, ending with his pediatrician, who called and met him on her supper break. The mother said the small gesture eased the move. Another: On the last day of school the daughter's best friend was moving away; she wished the family would move too, and asked to be left alone to cry. Her mother stayed available. Another: A New York Times Magazine piece on retirement: send-offs vary and the old gold-watch custom has mostly gone; some had parties, others regretted missed time with their children, and it is often sad. Another: A public relations worker left a nonprofit after nearly twenty years when leaders reversed promises about working from home. He would miss his supervisor of more than ten years and his work friends, and took a new job in six weeks.
